metadata.title: Migrate Content Extraction to Silver Layer

story.iWant: migrate content extraction to use raw HTML from bronze and output to silver layer
story.soThat: extracted content is properly layered and can be reprocessed from cached HTML
story.tasks: - Task 1: Create silver_extracted_content asset (AC: 1, 2, 3) - Task 2: Update html_extractor to read from bronze cache (AC: 4) - Task 3: Implement silver asset logic (AC: 2, 6) - Task 4: Verify SilverIOManager handles extracted content (AC: 3, 6, 7) - Task 5: Handle YouTube extraction (AC: 5) - Task 6: Update legacy asset references (AC: 1) - Task 7: Create integration tests (AC: 8, 9) - Task 8: Run all tests and quality checks (AC: 8, 9)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: AC1: content_extraction asset renamed to silver_extracted_content - Asset file exists with new name AC2: Asset depends on bronze_raw_html instead of fetching URLs directly - Function signature declares dependency parameter AC3: Asset configured to use SilverIOManager - Asset decorated with io_manager_key="silver_io_manager" AC4: HTML extractor op reads from bronze cache - html_extractor.py reads from cached JSON files AC5: YouTube extractor continues to use yt-dlp (no HTML caching for videos) - youtube_extractor.py unchanged, uses yt-dlp directly AC6: Extracted content includes full metadata with timestamps and lineage - JSON structure verified in tests AC7: Content stored in artifacts/silver/extracted_content/ with full hash filenames - Files saved with 64-char SHA256 hash AC8: Integration test verifies end-to-end flow from bronze HTML to silver content - End-to-end test passes AC9: Reprocessing test confirms can regenerate silver from bronze without re-download - Test deletes silver, re-runs from bronze, verifies no HTTP download

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Medallion Architecture Migration
doc.snippet: Defines silver extracted content data model with url, type, title, content, metadata (author, published_date, word_count, extraction_method), and lineage tracking. Specifies full SHA256 hash filenames and silver layer directory structure at artifacts/silver/extracted_content/.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Medallion Architecture Migration
doc.snippet: Defines silver_extracted_content asset signature: depends on bronze_raw_html (List[dict]), uses silver_io_manager, reads cached HTML from bronze layer, can be re-materialized without re-downloading HTML.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Medallion Architecture Migration
doc.section: Workflows and Sequencing - Asset Dependency Flow (lines 304-343)
doc.snippet: Shows bronze_raw_html → silver_extracted_content flow with file-based caching. silver_extracted_content reads from bronze cache (checks for cached files), enabling reprocessing: delete silver artifacts → re-run from bronze → no re-download.

doc.title: Architecture Documentation - DeepRock
doc.snippet: Medallion pattern separates data by maturity: bronze (raw, immutable) and silver (processed, application-ready). Silver layer applies business logic, validates quality, enriches metadata. File naming: {full_sha256_hash}.{extension}. All silver artifacts require created_at, updated_at, and lineage metadata.

doc.title: ailabbrains - Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 1.6: Migrate Content Extraction to Silver Layer (lines 136-154)
doc.snippet: Story requirements: rename content_extraction to silver_extracted_content, depend on bronze_raw_html, use SilverIOManager, html_extractor reads from bronze cache, YouTube extractor continues yt-dlp, include full metadata with lineage, integration tests verify end-to-end flow and reprocessing.

doc.title: Story 1.5: Add Raw HTML Download to Bronze Layer
doc.snippet: bronze_raw_html asset downloads and caches HTML in artifacts/bronze/raw_html/ with file-existence caching strategy. Returns List[dict] with url, html_content, download_info (status_code, headers, timestamp), error metadata for failures. Enables reprocessing workflows without re-download.

doc.title: Story 1.3: Implement Silver Layer IOManager
doc.snippet: SilverIOManager handles persistence of processed data to silver layer, adding created_at, updated_at timestamps and lineage metadata (source_asset, source_hash, transformation_timestamp). Supports content-type awareness for different data types (extracted content, summaries).

doc.title: Development Guide
doc.snippet: Integration tests required for multi-component flows, marked with @pytest.mark.integration, located in tests/integration/. Use PropertyMock for test configuration injection. All tests must pass before story completion (make check).

artifact.reason: HTML extraction logic that needs to be refactored - currently downloads via httpx.get(), should be modified to accept cached HTML from bronze layer instead of URL. BeautifulSoup parsing logic (lines 27-63) should be preserved.
Return type for HTML extraction - url, title, content, author, publish_date, metadata. This structure should be adapted for silver layer with lineage metadata added.
YouTube extraction logic using yt-dlp - should remain unchanged (no caching for videos). Will be called by silver_extracted_content for YouTube URLs.
Return type for YouTube extraction - url, title, transcript, description, channel, duration, metadata. This structure should be adapted for silver layer with lineage metadata.

Legacy asset to be migrated/replaced. Shows current pattern: depends on link_ingestion, dispatches to html_extractor or youtube_extractor, saves to artifacts/html/ or artifacts/videos/. This should be refactored to depend on bronze_raw_html and output to silver layer.

Upstream dependency - returns List[dict] with url, html_content, download_info (status_code, headers, timestamp), error metadata for failures. silver_extracted_content will read from this asset's output instead of downloading HTML directly.

Persistence logic for extracted content - expects dict with url, type, title, content, metadata, lineage. Adds created_at and updated_at timestamps. Saves to artifacts/silver/extracted_content/ with full SHA256 hash filename.
Bronze HTML storage - saves HTML with "content" field in JSON. silver_extracted_content will read from these cached files to extract content without re-downloading.
Asset exports for Dagster discovery - needs to be updated to export silver_extracted_content instead of (or in addition to) content_extraction_asset.

constraints.constraint: Use structlog for all logging (not print or context.log) - established pattern in bronze layer
Full SHA256 hash (64 chars) for all filenames - NO truncation [:16]
Return plain data structures (List[dict]) - IOManager handles persistence with metadata enrichment
All silver artifacts must include lineage metadata: {"source_asset": "bronze_raw_html", "source_hash": str, "transformation_timestamp": str (ISO 8601)}
Preserve BeautifulSoup parsing logic from html_extractor.py - only remove HTTP download code
YouTube extractor continues to use yt-dlp directly - no caching for videos (only HTML is cached in bronze layer)
Handle error metadata from bronze layer - URLs with errors should be skipped or handled gracefully with error propagation
Integration tests only - mark with @pytest.mark.integration, located in tests/integration/
Make check must pass (ruff format, ruff check, pytest) before story completion

tests.standards: Integration tests required for all multi-component flows. Mark tests with @pytest.mark.integration and place in tests/integration/ directory. Use PropertyMock on context.op_execution_context.op_config for test configuration injection (established pattern from Story 1.5). All tests must pass before story completion - verify with "make check" (runs ruff format, ruff check, pytest). No unit tests required unless complex logic warrants isolation (integration tests preferred per project standards).

test.idea: End-to-end bronze HTML to silver content flow: Create bronze cache with test HTML → materialize silver_extracted_content → verify extracted content saved to artifacts/silver/extracted_content/ with correct metadata structure (url, type, title, content, lineage, timestamps)

Reprocessing test: Create bronze cache → materialize silver_extracted_content → delete silver artifacts → re-materialize silver_extracted_content → verify httpx.get was NOT called (using mock), verify silver artifacts regenerated from bronze cache
HTML extractor reads from bronze cache: Mock bronze_raw_html output with cached HTML → verify html_extractor receives HTML content (not URL) → verify BeautifulSoup parsing works correctly

Metadata structure validation: Verify extracted content includes all required fields (url, type, title, content, metadata with author/published_date/word_count/extraction_method, lineage with source_asset/source_hash/transformation_timestamp)
YouTube extraction continues to work: Test YouTube URL → verify youtube_extractor called (not html_extractor) → verify yt-dlp used directly → verify output structure correct

Error handling from bronze layer: Create bronze cache with error metadata (failed HTTP download) → verify silver_extracted_content handles gracefully → verify error propagated or skipped appropriately
Full SHA256 hash filenames: Verify all saved files in artifacts/silver/extracted_content/ use 64-char SHA256 hash (not truncated [:16])
